reason: Isolate the uplink to rehearse whether the local rack works without Meridian.
expectation: I expect the shared controls to be disconnected from the uplink so their local operation can be tested, though the result may reveal a dependency.

alternatives.reason: Testing the clinic link also supports the rehearsal, but I want to isolate the uplink first.

effect: The uplink is disconnected, but the green door indicator alone does not verify the other local paths.
reaction: The warning against trusting a single indicator is useful.
reason: The handset test is the only available combination and can check the clinic radio link offline.
expectation: I expect the handset to test communication over the clinic link without the outside connection; it may reveal a remaining dependency.

effect: The radio link works, but clinic address discovery still depends on the company directory; the controller is the next place to address that dependency.
reaction: The independent road and missing signpost is a clear, surprising failure.
reason: The controller is the only available combination and may provide a local way to find the clinic.
expectation: I expect to configure or reveal a local clinic address on the controller, though another test may be needed.

effect: The handset now carries local directory settings and can configure the disconnected rack through its service port.
reaction: The limited local directory makes sense; it doesn't pretend to replace the internet.
reason: Use the only available combination to configure the rack with the local settings.
expectation: I expect the rack to receive the local directory settings, though the clinic call will still need testing.

effect: The rack now runs its own service directory without the uplink, completing the first goal; the remaining paths still need checking.
reaction: Satisfying to see the missing directory brought under local control.
reason: The only available combination may test the handset against the rack's new directory.
expectation: I expect the handset to find local services through the rack, though the clinic call and water service may need further checks.

effect: The handset now resolves the clinic locally and reaches Eli without the uplink; water service remains to be checked.
reaction: The callback is a nice, concrete confirmation that the directory fix worked.
reason: Use the only available combination to check the water service alongside the working clinic call.
expectation: I expect a rehearsal check of the water service while the clinic remains reachable, though it may reveal another dependency.

effect: The stop-and-restart test confirmed that local pump control, water flow and clinic communication survived without the uplink; both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The coordinated test was a satisfying confirmation beyond a green indicator.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the handset after disconnecting the uplink was most worthwhile: it exposed a company directory dependency despite the radios still working.

leastWorthwhile.text: Loading the settings onto the handset and then the rack felt like a somewhat procedural sequence, especially with only one combination offered at each step.

surprise.text: The clinic call depended on a corporate directory even though the local radios could still exchange packets. The road-and-signpost analogy made the failure clear.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the handset's role in transferring settings to the rack only became clear after the combination.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see whether the neighborhood's local systems hold up during migration; uncovering and testing the hidden directory dependency made this chapter engaging.
